scope: local ARM64 kernel build, generic QEMU and disposable Arch ARM initramfs; no Apple hardware test
toolchain: Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 VM, clang 18.1.3, GNU ld 2.42, Rust 1.99.0, bindgen 0.71.1
build: Fresh out-of-tree --r7 --arch-research --rootfix build, started with four jobs and safely resumed with six jobs after source and configuration rechecking.
staging: All modules.order entries staged; key module vermagic matched the release and depmod -e with System.map returned no diagnostics. The Arch-shaped package was built with dependency resolution skipped and has not been installed on a Mac.

qemu.scope: generic ARM64 virt machine, HVF, no disks or network; no Apple devices
qemu.result: Booted and loaded asahi_m4, appledrm, phy_apple_dptx, nvme_apple, dm_crypt and dm_integrity without hardware present.

arch_arm_initramfs.scope: signed generic Arch Linux ARM root in an isolated VM, partially updated, with Omarchy boot payload and Asahi hooks staged manually; modules are not package-owned in this test
arch_arm_initramfs.result: Both images built without errors; each included the storage and encryption modules, their modprobe dependency closures, cryptsetup and firmware helpers. A generated cryptsetup unit and the Omarchy services passed offline systemd verification.
warnings: fallback also warned about xhci_pci_renesas and ufs_renesas firmware

limitations: no M4 mini boot or HDMI test
no verified firmware handoff or GPU execution
no qualified package transaction or recovery path
generic VM tests do not establish Apple hardware compatibility
